method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline' (published 1 January 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © 2025 American Academy of Sleep Medicine (no open licence; PMC not open access) (read at PMC efetch XML <permissions> element for PMC11701286). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Only the guideline's structured abstract was readable: the PMC XML carries no body, and the PMC and JCSM article pages returned bot challenges, which were not bypassed. The abstract states the good practice statements and all 28 recommendations in full; the evidence review, remarks beyond those in the abstract, and doses are not available.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check iron in everyone with clinically significant RLS:** ferritin and transferrin saturation, ideally a morning sample with no iron supplements or iron-rich food for at least 24 hours beforehand. The result decides between oral and IV iron.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Iron thresholds for RLS are higher than for the general population.** Adults: replace iron (oral or IV) at ferritin ≤ 75 ng/mL or a transferrin saturation under 20%; use only IV iron at ferritin 75 to 100 ng/mL. In children, supplement when ferritin is < 50 ng/mL. These consensus thresholds are untested.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start by removing aggravating factors:** alcohol, caffeine, antihistaminergic, serotonergic and antidopaminergic drugs, and untreated obstructive sleep apnoea.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **RLS is common in pregnancy;** weigh the pregnancy safety of each option before prescribing.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Gabapentinoids are the preferred drugs:** gabapentin enacarbil, gabapentin and pregabalin each carry a strong recommendation (moderate certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV ferric carboxymaltose is strongly recommended** when iron status meets the thresholds above (moderate certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other iron preparations are suggested when iron status fits:** IV low molecular weight iron dextran or IV ferumoxytol (very low certainty), or oral ferrous sulfate (moderate certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Opioids, including extended-release oxycodone, are a suggested option** (moderate certainty); dipyridamole is also suggested (low certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bilateral high-frequency peroneal nerve stimulation is a suggested non-drug option** (moderate certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pramipexole is not advised for standard use** (conditional, moderate certainty). It may still suit someone who values short-term symptom relief over long-term harms, especially augmentation.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The same applies to ropinirole (moderate certainty), transdermal rotigotine (low certainty) and levodopa (very low certainty):** not for standard use, only where short-term relief is valued over the risk of augmentation.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use cabergoline** (strong recommendation against, moderate certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bupropion (moderate certainty), carbamazepine and valproic acid (low certainty), and clonazepam and valerian (very low certainty) are advised against** for RLS.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **End-stage renal disease:** gabapentin (very low certainty), vitamin C (low certainty) and IV iron sucrose when ferritin is < 200 ng/mL and transferrin saturation < 20% (moderate certainty) are suggested.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **End-stage renal disease:** levodopa and rotigotine are likewise not for standard use, for the same augmentation reason.
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children with RLS:** oral ferrous sulfate is suggested when iron status fits (very low certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Periodic limb movement disorder in adults:** triazolam and valproic acid are advised against (very low certainty).
claims.locator: American Academy of Sleep Medicine task force (Winkelman JW, Berkowski JA, DelRosso LM, et al.), Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine 21(1):137–152, doi 10.5664/jcsm.11390, 'Treatment of restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movement disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline', published 1 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11701286/, retrieved 2026-09-23
